messages.subject: legends
parts:
Hi

Is there a way to add a second legend to a plot? Or is there a way to
use more than one grouping variable? I simply want to plot 6 lines,
which need to be identified by treatment (3 lines) and group within
treatment (2 lines for each of the 3 treatments). I'm using symbols
for the treatment and 2 different line types for the groups within
treatment.
Thanks for any suggestions.

Hi Henrik,

The problem is that you're setting shape to multiple values which
isn't what you're supposed to do (and will be an error in a future
version). Please make a small reproducible example (perhaps using a
subset of your data) and send it to the mailing list. Then people can
suggest alternatives.

Hadley

messages.subject: legends
parts:
I'm trying to plot 6 lines, which need to be identified by main group
(3 lines) and sub-group (2 lines for each of the 3 main groups). I'm
using symbols for the main group and 2 different line types for the
sub-groups.

ggplot() +
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=controls,fun.y=mean, geom='line',size=0.5,
linetype='dashed') +
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=treatment,fun.y=mean, geom='line',size=0.5) +
# error bars
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=controls,fun.data='mean_cl_normal', geom='errorbar',
width=0.1) +
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=treatment,fun.data='mean_cl_normal', geom='errorbar',
width=0.1) +
# symbols
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=controls,fun.y=mean, geom='point', size=3, shape=c
(22,21,24), fill='white') +
stat_summary(aes(x,y, group=a,colour=a),
data=otc,fun.y=mean, geom='point', size=3, shape=c(15,16,17))
+
# X & Y labels
xlab('Time') + ylab('Response')
